cited_text.Annex III(4)(a): (a) AI systems intended to be used for the recruitment or selection of natural persons, in particular to place targeted job advertisements, to analyse and filter job applications, and to evaluate candidates;
cited_text.Art 6(2): 2. In addition to the high-risk AI systems referred to in paragraph 1, AI systems referred to in Annex III shall be considered to be high-risk.

key_facts: The tool screens and ranks job applicants' CVs
It shortlists the top candidates for recruiters
output.rationale: The tool analyses and filters job applications and evaluates candidates for recruitment, which is a listed Annex III employment use case. That makes it high-risk. Recruiters act on the shortlist, but the use case is listed regardless of that human step.

obligations.text: Establish, implement, document and maintain a risk management system.
Develop the system using training, validation and testing data sets that meet the data quality criteria.
Draw up and keep up to date technical documentation before placing on the market or putting into service.
Ensure the system technically allows automatic recording of events (logs) over its lifetime.
Design the system to be sufficiently transparent for deployers to interpret and use its output.
Accompany the system with instructions for use containing the required information for deployers.
Design the system so natural persons can effectively oversee it while in use.
Ensure an appropriate level of accuracy, robustness and cybersecurity throughout the lifecycle.
Complete the internal-control conformity assessment procedure (Annex VI) before placing on the market.
Register the provider and the system in the EU database before placing on the market or putting into service.

to_confirm: Confirm the tool is placed on the market or put into service in the EU, or its output is used in the EU.
Confirm whether you are the provider (developer) or only a deployer, as the obligations differ.

cited_text.Art 50(1): 1. Providers shall ensure that AI systems intended to interact directly with natural persons are designed and developed in such a way that the natural persons concerned are informed that they are interacting with an AI system, unless this is obvious from the point of view of a natural person who is reasonably well-informed, observant and circumspect, taking into account the circumstances and the context of use. This obligation shall not apply to AI systems authorised by law to detect, prevent, investigate or prosecute criminal offences, subject to appropriate safeguards for the rights and freedoms of third parties, unless those systems are available for the public to report a criminal offence.

key_facts: Customer-service chatbot on an e-commerce website
Answers shopper questions in natural language
output.rationale: The chatbot talks directly with people, so it falls under the transparency rules for AI systems that interact with natural persons. Answering shopper questions on an e-commerce site is not an Annex III high-risk purpose, and nothing in the description suggests a prohibited practice. The main duty is to make sure users know they are talking to an AI, unless that is obvious from the context.

obligations.text: Design and develop the chatbot so users are informed they are interacting with an AI system, unless this is obvious to a reasonably well-informed person from the context.

to_confirm: Confirm the chatbot is not also used for high-risk purposes, such as credit assessment of shoppers.
Confirm the chatbot does not use manipulative or exploitative techniques.
Confirm whether the chatbot generates synthetic text that is published to inform the public, which would trigger further transparency duties.

key_facts: Government system scores each citizen's trustworthiness from everyday behaviour
The score is used to grant or deny access to public services
output.rationale: The system evaluates people over time based on their social behaviour and uses the resulting score to deny them public services. That is social scoring, which Art 5(1)(c) prohibits. Denial of services is detrimental treatment, and it can occur in contexts unrelated to where the data was collected or can be disproportionate to the behaviour.

obligations.text: Do not develop, place on the market, put into service or use this social scoring system.

to_confirm: Confirm that the score does lead to detrimental treatment that is unrelated to the original data context or is disproportionate to the behaviour. Denial of public services on this basis would meet that test.

cited_text.Art 6(2): 2. In addition to the high-risk AI systems referred to in paragraph 1, AI systems referred to in Annex III shall be considered to be high-risk.
cited_text.Annex III(5)(b): (b) AI systems intended to be used to evaluate the creditworthiness of natural persons or establish their credit score, with the exception of AI systems used for the purpose of detecting financial fraud;

key_facts: The model scores loan applicants' creditworthiness
The bank uses the score to decide who gets a loan
output.rationale: The system evaluates the creditworthiness of natural persons, which is an Annex III high-risk use case. The use is credit scoring rather than fraud detection, so the fraud exception does not apply. The full high-risk requirements apply.

to_confirm: Confirm the system scores natural persons (individual applicants), not only businesses.
Confirm the system is not used solely to detect financial fraud.

key_facts: The system does real-time facial recognition of people in public squares
The feed is streamed to the police
output.rationale: This is a 'real-time' remote biometric identification system used in publicly accessible spaces for law enforcement. Art 5(1)(h) prohibits that unless the use is strictly necessary for a narrow listed objective, such as searching for victims or missing persons, preventing an imminent threat, or locating a suspect of a serious Annex II offence. The description describes general streaming of public squares to police, not a targeted use within those exceptions, so it falls under the prohibition.

obligations.text: Do not develop, place on the market, put into service or use this system for real-time remote biometric identification in public spaces for law enforcement.

to_confirm: Whether any use is strictly limited to one of the Art 5(1)(h) objectives (targeted search for victims or missing persons, imminent threat, or a serious Annex II suspect). Such use would also need national-law authorisation, a fundamental rights impact assessment and EU database registration under Art 5(2).
Whether the system identifies people continuously and indiscriminately, or only confirms the identity of a specifically targeted individual.

cited_text.Art 2(8): 8. This Regulation does not apply to any research, testing or development activity regarding AI systems or AI models prior to their being placed on the market or put into service. Such activities shall be conducted in accordance with applicable Union law. Testing in real world conditions shall not be covered by that exclusion.

key_facts: Internal research model trained and tested in the lab only
output.rationale: The Act does not apply to research, testing or development of AI systems or models before they are placed on the market or put into service. Your model stays in the lab and is not tested on real users, so the exclusion applies. The exclusion would no longer cover it if it were released, put into service, or tested in real-world conditions.
to_confirm: The model stays internal and is never put into service, including for your own operational use.
No testing in real-world conditions is planned, because that is not covered by the exclusion.
The research and development activity still complies with other applicable Union law, such as data protection.
